rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrisy, like apostasy, can arise after a person has believed; al-Rūm 30:10 connects evil deeds with a disastrous end of denial of God's signs.
rows.anchor: وثانيا أن من النفاق ما يعرض الإنسان بعد الإيمان كما أن من الكفر ما هو كذلك وهو الردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-najwā means concealed or private speech.
rows.anchor: النجوى الكلام الخفي والاستفهام للتوبيخ والتأنيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes and reproaches those being addressed.
rows.anchor: النجوى الكلام الخفي والاستفهام للتوبيخ والتأنيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Voluntary giving is an act the soul does not dislike or regard as burdensome, so the term commonly denotes recommended acts rather than obligations that one may resent having to perform.
rows.anchor: التطوع الإتيان بما لا تكرهه النفس ولا تحسبه شاقا ولذلك يستعمل غالبا في المندوبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrasting voluntary donors with people who have only their utmost effort, the verse points to well-off believers giving zakat freely and without hardship, unlike the poor who give what strains their means.
rows.anchor: ومقابلة المطوعين من المؤمنين في الصدقات بالذين لا يجدون إلا جهدهم قرينة على أن المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may stand independently, or describe the people introduced at 9:75; the passage then criticizes their abuse of both wealthy and poor donors.
rows.anchor: كلام مستأنف أو هو وصف للذين ذكروا بقوله { ومنهم من عاهد الله } الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mockers disparage every donor, rich or poor; God's mockery of them and painful punishment answer their ridicule and threaten severe retribution.
rows.anchor: فيعيبون المتصدقين موسرهم ومعسرهم وغنيهم وفقيرهم ويسخرون منهم سخر الله منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command-or-prohibition wording implies that seeking forgiveness and refraining from it have the same futile result, as in 9:53.
rows.anchor: الترديد بين الأمر والنهي كناية عن تساوي الفعل والترك أي لغوية الفعل كما مر نظيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are another group of sinful Bedouins, unlike the hypocrites: they acknowledged their sins and mixed good deeds with bad, so God's turning to them remains possible.
rows.anchor: أي ومن الأعراب جماعة آخرون مذنبون لا ينافقون مثل غيرهم بل اعترفوا بذنوبهم لهم عمل صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording instills hope so their souls remain between fear and hope rather than falling into despair.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم } إيجاد الرجاء في نفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God forgiving and merciful gives greater weight to hope.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { إن الله غفور رحيم } ترجيح جانب الرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification removes dirt and defilement so a thing becomes clear and ready for growth and the appearance of its effects and blessings.
rows.anchor: التطهير إزالة الأوساخ والقذارات من الشيء ليصفى وجوده ويستعد للنشوء والنماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiya means growth and guidance through the arrival of good and the appearance of blessings, like pruning a tree to improve its growth and fruit.
rows.anchor: والتزكية إنماؤه وإعطاء الرشد له بلحوق الخيرات وظهور البركات كالشجرة بقطع الزوائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining purification and growth is an especially subtle expression, joining removal of impediments with flourishing.
rows.anchor: فالجمع بين التطهير والتزكية في الآية من لطيف التعبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural 'their properties' signals that the charity is taken from different kinds of wealth: gold and silver, camels, cattle and sheep, and wheat, barley, dates and raisins.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل من مالهم ليكون إشارة إلى أنها مأخوذة من أصناف المال، وهي النقدان الذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs address the Prophet, rather than describe the charity itself: the pronoun in 'by it' refers to charity, meaning he purifies and develops them through taking it.
rows.anchor: وليس وصفا لحال الصدقة، والدليل عليه ضمير بها الراجع إلى الصدقة أي خذ يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praying for donors means supplicating for good and blessing for them and their property, as the Prophet's established practice shows.
rows.anchor: الصلاة عليهم هي الدعاء لهم والسياق يفيد أنه دعاء لهم ولأموالهم بالخير والبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donors' souls find reassurance and trust in the Prophet's prayer; it also thanks them for their service to God.
rows.anchor: المراد به أن نفوسهم تسكن إلى دعائك وتثق به وهو نوع شكر لسعيهم في الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing assurance that God hears and knows likewise reassures those charged with religious duties who hear or recite the verse.
rows.anchor: سكن يسكن إليه نفوس المكلفين ممن يسمع الآية أو يتلوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes financial zakat as an obligation and one of the pillars of the religious law; abundant reports from the Imams of the Prophet's family and others explain it this way.
rows.anchor: والآية تتضمن حكم الزكاة المالية التي هي من أركان الشريعة والملة على ما هو ظاهر الآية

words: يَقْبَلُ ٱلتَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَأْخُذُ ٱلصَّدَقَٰتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is a rebuke designed to encourage people to give zakat.
rows.anchor: استفهام إنكاري بداعي تشويق الناس إلى إيتاء الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true recipient: people hand charity to the Prophet or his authorized collector, so giving to the agent is giving to God and his taking is God's taking.
rows.anchor: فالله سبحانه هو الآخذ لها بالحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People know only the outward appearance of their deeds until resurrection; the believers who see their realities before then are witnesses of deeds, not all believers, as 2:143 indicates.
rows.anchor: وكان المراد بالمؤمنين شهداء الأعمال منهم لا عامة المؤمنين كما يدل عليه أمثال قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse calls people to monitor their deeds: God, the Messenger and witnesses of deeds see their realities in this life, and on resurrection the actors themselves are shown them.
rows.anchor: فإن حقيقته مرئية مشهودة لله عالم الغيب والشهادة ثم لرسوله والمؤمنين في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that God will uncover deeds' reality at resurrection is illustrated by 50:22, when the veil is removed and sight becomes sharp.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الله سبحانه سيكشف عنها الغطاء يوم القيامة للعاملين أنفسهم كما قال لقد كنت في غفلة من هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example contrasts an act done in private under the impression no one sees with the same act performed publicly among witnesses.
rows.anchor: ففرق عظيم بين أن يأتي الإنسان بعمل في الخلوة لا يطلع عليه أحد، وبين أن يعمل ذلك العمل بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding passage addresses particular hypocrites: God tells the Prophet to reject their excuses and says revelation has exposed their deeds to him and the believers with him.
rows.anchor: فإن وجه الكلام فيها إلى أشخاص من المنافقين بأعيانهم يأمر الله فيها نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse was revealed about ʿAlī: he was first to believe, prayed toward both qiblas, joined the pledges of Badr and al-Riḍwān, and migrated twice with Jaʿfar, to Abyssinia and then Medina.
rows.anchor: عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس قال { والسابقون الأولون } نزلت في أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

rows.speaker: جماعة من أصحاب النبي
rows.claim: A group of Companions report that the Prophet said this verse applied to his whole community and that no displeasure follows the stated divine approval.
rows.anchor: أنهم سمعوا جماعة من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقولون لما أنزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects reading the report as approval of the entire community: the verse's approval concerns the people it specifies, and 'no displeasure after approval' means the approval stated here, not every divine approval.
rows.anchor: لا أن الآية تدل على رضاه تعالى عن الأمة كلهم فهذا مما يدفعه الكتاب بالمخالفة القطعية

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Quraẓī argues that God promised Paradise and forgiveness to all Companions, virtuous and sinful, while requiring later followers to emulate their good deeds but not their other conduct.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صخر فوالله لكأني لم اقرأها قبل ذلك، وما عرفت تفسيرها حتى قرأها علي محمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that all Companions' good and bad deeds are forgiven without consequence: it contradicts verses denying God's approval, love or guidance to wrongdoers and the Qur'an's general rule of recompense.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي ذكرنا في البيان المتقدم أن مقتضاه تكذيب آيات كثيرة قرآنية تدل على أن الله لا يرضى عن القوم الفاسقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse meant unconditional approval of every Companion, their Arabic fluency and closeness to revelation should have made them understand it; recorded conflicts and mutual disapproval are incompatible with that reading, and appeal to ijtihad cannot reconcile the contradiction.
rows.anchor: وكيف يمكن أن يتحقق كلهم بمضمون قوله { رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه } ويفهموا ذلك منه ثم لا يرضى بعضهم عن بعض

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: A report says ʿUmar recited al-Anṣār in the nominative and omitted the conjunction waw before 'those who followed'; Zayd corrected him, and Ubayy confirmed the wording with waw.
rows.anchor: عن حبيب الشهيد عن عمرو بن عامر الأنصاري أن عمر بن الخطاب قرأ { والسابقون الأولون من المهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوهم بإحسان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On ʿUmar's reading, the special merit in 'the foremost' belongs to the Emigrants, who also have the merit of being followed by the Anṣār.
rows.anchor: ومقتضى قراءة عمر اختصاص المهاجرين بما يتضمنه قوله { والسابقون الأولون } من المنقبة

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy confirms to ʿUmar that he heard the wording with waw from the Prophet, then cites 62:3, 59:10 and 8:75 to show later believers can join the earlier community through following and faith.
rows.anchor: قال أبي تصديق ذلك في أول سورة الجمعة { وآخرين منهم لما يلحقوا بهم }

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from Imam al-Bāqir identifies them as believers who commit sins that believers disapprove of and dislike, for whom God's turning remains possible.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر عليه السلام { الذين خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا } فأولئك قوم مؤمنون يحدثون

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī's report from Zurāra gives the same explanation but has 'sinners' in place of 'believers'.
rows.anchor: ورواه العياشي عن زرارة عنه عليه السلام إلا أن فيه { مذنبون } { مكان مؤمنون }

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
rows.claim: Abū Ḥamza al-Thumālī says he was told that three Anṣār—Abū Kināna, Thaʿlaba b. Wadīʿa and Aws b. Ḥidhām—stayed behind at Tabūk, bound themselves to mosque pillars in remorse, and awaited the Prophet's return and release.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حمزة الثمالي بلغنا أنهم ثلاثة نفر من الأنصار أبو كنانة بن عبد المنذر وثعلبة بن وديعة

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
rows.claim: In Abū Ḥamza's account, the Prophet would not release the three men first without a divine instruction; after this verse was revealed, he freed them, and they offered the wealth that had kept them back as charity, but he said he had not been ordered to take it.
rows.anchor: وأنا أقسم لا أكون أول من حلهم إلا أن أومر فيهم بأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports differ over the men's names and say the charity verse concerned their specific wealth; the author considers that account weak because many reports show the verse concerns obligatory zakat.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى روايات أخرى رواها في الدر المنثور بينها اختلاف في أسامي الرجال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed about Abū Lubāba alone, after he told Banū Qurayẓa that surrendering to the Prophet's judgment meant slaughter.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر الباقر عليه السلام أنها نزلت في أبي لبابة ولم يذكر غيره معه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Sinān reports from Imam al-Ṣādiq that in Ramadan the Prophet announced zakat as obligatory like prayer, specifying gold, silver, camels, cattle, sheep, wheat, barley, dates and raisins, and exempting other property.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن عبد الله بن سنان قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام لما نزلت هذه الآية { خذ من أموالهم صدقة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The same report says no further wealth obligation was imposed until a year had passed; after the first Ramadan fast, the Prophet's caller urged Muslims to purify their wealth so their prayers would be accepted, and collectors were dispatched.
rows.anchor: ثم لم يفرض لشيء من أموالهم حتى حال عليه الحول من قابل فصاموا وأفطروا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Awfā reports that when someone brought charity the Prophet prayed for that person's family; when Ibn Abī Awfā's father brought his charity, he prayed for the family of Abī Awfā.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتي بصدقة قال اللهم صل على آل فلان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Ṣādiq explains 'He takes the charities' to mean that God accepts them from their people and rewards them for it.
rows.anchor: عن سليمان بن مهران عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { ويأخذ الصدقات } قال يقبلها من أهلها

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn says he has guaranteed from his Lord that charity reaches God's hand before a servant's, interpreting the verse's statement that God accepts repentance and takes charities.
rows.anchor: عن مالك بن عطية عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قال علي بن الحسين عليه السلام ضمنت على ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam assigns society a share in wealth's benefits through obligations such as zakat and khums; this answers society's need for resources and resembles provisions in earlier law codes and customary systems.
rows.anchor: وقد عزلت الشريعة الإسلامية سهما من منافع الأموال وفوائدها للمجتمع كالصدقة الواجبة التي هي الزكاة وكالخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first distinctive feature is that zakat and similar shares attach when new wealth arises, such as harvest or trading profit, and the remaining shares belong to the owner or worker.
rows.anchor: أنها اقتصرت في وضع هذا النوع من الجهات المالية على كينونة الملك وحدوثه موجودا ولم يتعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests 2:29 and 4:5 may imply that newly arising wealth first belongs wholly to society, after which a share is assigned to the individual; zakat or khums remains society's share, while the individual owns the rest.
rows.anchor: خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once ownership has settled, Islam imposes no further claim on the owner's property merely because of conditions or circumstances; charges on persons, land or commerce at special times are treated as usurpation, except emergencies threatening society's survival.
rows.anchor: وأما إذا انعقد الملك واستقر لمالكه فلا اعتراض لمعترض على مالك في حال أو عند شرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second feature favors individuals in distributing public shares: zakat has eight categories, only one for God's cause, while the others serve people; khums has six shares, with five assigned to the Prophet, kin, orphans, needy and travelers.
rows.anchor: فإنه يجعل السهام في الزكاة ثمانية لا يختص بسبيل الله منها إلا سهم واحد وباقي السهام للأفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because individuals are society's constituent elements, reducing class differences and balancing social forces requires improving individuals and bringing their circumstances closer; spending communal wealth on prestige projects while rich and poor diverge does not solve social harm.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الفرد هو العنصر الوحيد لتكون المجتمع، ورفع اختلاف الطبقات الذي هو من أصول برنامج الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third, a Muslim may in some circumstances pay obligatory zakat directly to eligible poor or needy recipients rather than route it through the ruler or collector.
rows.anchor: أن للفرد من المسلمين أن يصرف ما عليه من الحق المالي الواجب كالزكاة مثلا في بعض أرباب السهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This direct-distribution right reflects the independence Islam grants individuals, like the authority to give safe conduct to hostile non-Muslims; the ruler may prohibit it when public Muslim interests require, and must be obeyed.
rows.anchor: وهذا نوع من الاحترام الاستقلالي الذي اعتبره الإسلام لأفراد مجتمعه نظير إعطاء الذمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud that the people of ʿĀd mistook for rain is linked with the punishment they had demanded, as 46:24 describes.
rows.anchor: فلما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم قالوا هذا عارض ممطرنا بل هو ما استعجلتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human conduct is closely connected to cosmic events: righteous deeds bring abundant good and blessings, while evil deeds draw calamities, divine punishment, misery and ruin; 7:96 is a parallel, discussed earlier in volumes eight and two.
rows.anchor: أن هناك ارتباطا تاما بين الأعمال الإنسانية وبين الحوادث الكونية التي تمسه فالأعمال الصالحة توجب فيضان الخيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Hūd answer in general that he brought no proof or miraculous sign, so there is no reason to heed a call they consider unsupported.
rows.anchor: يعنون أن دعوتك خالية عن الحجة والآية المعجزة ولا موجب للإصغاء إلى ما هذا شأنه

words: وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَارِكِىٓ ءَالِهَتِنَا عَن قَوْلِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specifically, they refuse to abandon their partners, and refuse to believe in or obey Hūd, rejecting both parts of his appeal.
rows.anchor: فآيسوه في كلتا المسألتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-iʿtirāʾ means to assault or afflict someone.
rows.anchor: والاعتراء الاعتراض والإصابة يقولون إنما نعتقد في أمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim one of their gods afflicted Hūd with madness for insulting it, leaving him irrational and making his preaching unworthy of attention.
rows.anchor: إنما نعتقد في أمرك أن بعض آلهتنا أصابك بسوء كالخبل والجنون لشتمك إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd's declaration of innocence is a performative act, appropriate to renunciation, even though he had been innocent from the beginning.
rows.anchor: إنشاء وليس بإخبار كما هو المناسب لمقام التبري، ولا ينافي ذلك كونه بريئا من أول أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to plot and prohibition on delaying are deliberately impossible challenges.
rows.anchor: أمر ونهي تعجيزيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd challenges them so they can see that their gods neither harm him nor avenge themselves; their inaction proves the gods are powerless and did not afflict him.
rows.anchor: ولو كانت آلهة ذات علم وقدرة لقهرته وانتقمت منه لنفسها كما ادعوا أن بعض آلهتهم اعتراه بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also see that despite their strength they cannot kill or punish Hūd; if he were not God's truthful prophet and protected by Him, they could have harmed him.
rows.anchor: ثم يشاهدوا من أنفسهم أنهم لا يقدرون عليه بقتل أو تنكيل مع كونهم ذوي شدة وقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd calls God to witness to attest that his renunciation is sincere, and calls his people to witness so they can observe their gods' silence and their own inability to retaliate.
rows.anchor: أما إشهاده الله فليكون تبريه على حقيقته وعن ظهر القلب من غير تزويق ونفاق
